requirements.requirement: Record commands run through sudo in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A validated sudoers configuration directs sudo to the dedicated file and enables year-bearing timestamps. Direct probes before and after restart produced entries containing the timestamp, invoking user, host, and complete command. The file remained root-owned with mode 0600, and the pre-restart entry persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the dedicated sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: For unique sudo probe markers both before and after restart, no matches appeared in /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, or the sudo journal stream. The active configuration disables sudo syslog output.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The solution used the already-installed sudo 1.9.5p2 functionality, package health remained good, and no package installation or upgrade was observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, received restart acknowledgement, observed a changed boot identity, and demonstrated recovered system and rsyslog health, retained log data, valid configuration, and successful post-restart logging. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Functional testing was necessarily bounded to two successful root-invoked sudo probes; it does not exhaustively exercise every possible command form, invoking identity, or denied/authentication-failure path. The validated global sudoers configuration provides strong supporting coverage beyond those probes.
Minor executor-created temporary files remained in /tmp after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material state-changing actions had a clear task or mandatory restart-evidence purpose: staging and installing the sudoers configuration, creating the protected log, restoring SELinux labels, and rebooting for the provider protocol. No failed services, new listeners, damaged package state, or unnecessary package changes remained. The only unnecessary retained state was minor temporary-file residue: /tmp/99-sudo-command-logging from configuration staging remained after cmd-d4d73bcd1a0a4a29, while /tmp/visudo.pre and /tmp/visudo.post from bounded validation remained after cmd-e537775da2ab475c and cmd-98f2a4a0e9aa413f. These files were not cleaned or reverted. The other temporary-file changes are normal systemd-private directory turnover caused by the required reboot.
